title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a complete smooth curve over a finite field k, with generic point η. E_η is an ℓ-adic (or torsion) representation of Gal(η̄/η). This is the 'geometric case' of the functional equation of L-functions.

The top two lines finish an argument from the previous page. They say the result is independent of the choice of a lift φ' of φ, presumably because only the factors of a composition series matter.

Local data. For each closed point x ∈ X:
- D_x is the decomposition group and I_x the inertia group.
- D_x/I_x ≅ π_x = Gal(k(x)‾/k(x)) ≅ Ẑ, generated by the Frobenius F_x.
- He sets E_η(x) := E_η^{I_x}, the inertia invariants, regarded as a π_x-module. This is the stalk at x of the Galois-module extension of E_η across x.

The identity. In the Grothendieck group K of (virtual) sheaves on X he writes
E_η^♮ = i_!(E_U) + Σ_{x∈Y} j_{x*}(E_η^{I(x)}),
where:
- E_η^♮ is the extension of E_η to all of X, i.e. g_*E_η = i_*E_U on a curve; the superscript is illegible.
- U is a dense open set on which E_η is unramified, and E_U is the corresponding lisse sheaf.
- Y = X − U; i: U → X and j: Y → X are the canonical immersions; j_x: Spec k(x) → X.

This is the class of the exact sequence
0 → i_!E_U → i_*E_U → ⊕_{x∈Y} (j_x)_*(E_η^{I_x}) → 0.
The sequence holds because the stalk of i_*E_U at x ∈ Y is E_η^{I_x}.

Purpose. It reduces the L-function of the extended sheaf to that of i_!E_U times the local Euler factors det(1 − F_x t | E^{I_x})^{-1} at the bad points. That is the standard first step toward the rationality and functional equation via the Lefschetz trace formula, Poincaré duality for i_* = j_{!*}, and the Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula for the ε-factor.
errors: No mathematical error. The notation is loose: E_η(x) for x ∈ U is the same as the unramified stalk. The superscript on the left-hand side (φ/ψ/♮) is unclear but must denote the extension of E_η to X (direct image from the generic point).

ideas.what: Stalk of the extended sheaf at a ramified point = inertia invariants, viewed as a Frobenius module
ideas.modern_name: Stalks of j_*F / intermediate extension on a curve; local L-factor det(1−F_x t | E^{I_x})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 4½ / SGA 5, Bourbaki exp. 279, 1964); analogue of Artin/Weil L-functions

ideas.modern_name: Excision / additivity in K_0 of constructible sheaves
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 (exposés on L-functions and the Euler–Poincaré formula)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard setup for the L-function of j_*E on a curve over a finite field, already in Grothendieck's 1964 Bourbaki talk and SGA 5. Nothing on the page is novel.
transcription_corrections: 'comme module[?] sur π_x' likely reads 'considéré comme module sur π_x'.

'Il vient alors = , dans K des classes de faisceaux virtuels sur X, de genre[?]' likely reads roughly 'Il vient alors, dans le groupe K des classes de faisceaux virtuels sur X, la formule'. 'de genre' is doubtful.
The left-hand side superscript 'E_η^φ' is uncertain; it plausibly denotes the canonical extension of E_η to X (direct image from the generic point), not φ.
The neighbouring pages are a Bourbaki typescript (Algèbre commutative ch. VII, Dedekind/Krull modules) on the reverse sides and are unrelated to this page.
